inline-links-color-only-no-other-cue: Links inside paragraphs are shown only by a different color with no underline or bold, so a color-blind user can't tell which words are clickable links.
required-field-color-only: A form marks required fields only by red color (and any instruction just says 'required fields are red'), so a color-blind user can't tell which are mandatory.
error-validation-color-only: After a failed submit, a wrong field is marked only by a red border or text, with no icon or message, so a color-blind user can't find it.
image-chart-alt-omits-color-encoded-fact: A chart's alt text restates the color rule ('red bars are below quota') but never says which items those are, so a blind user misses the color-coded fact.
color-coded-graphics-no-pattern-or-label: A chart, map, or diagram tells categories apart only by fill color with no patterns, shapes, or labels, so a color-blind user can't distinguish the routes or series.
ui-status-action-color-only-no-text-cue: A button or status uses color alone to mean go-versus-cancel or success-versus-error, with no distinguishing text, so a color-blind user can't tell which action it is.
scoping-non-failures-and-escape-hatches: Borderline color cases a naive 'any color use fails' rule gets wrong: enough lightness difference passes, hue-dependent meaning fails even at high contrast, and visited-link color is exempt.
